label: Person
name: Albert Privet Thévenot
summary:
Albert Privet (sometimes Privet-Thévenot) was a French Catholic bishop who served in the French colonial Catholic mission, representing the period of French missionary expansion in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries when French religious orders and secular clergy extended the Church's presence across France's colonial empire in Africa, Asia, and Oceania.

French missionaries and bishops were central to the Catholic Church's expansion in the colonial era. The Paris Foreign Missions Society (MEP), the White Fathers (Missionaries of Africa), and other French congregations conducted extensive missions that established Catholic communities across the French empire. Bishops like Privet-Thévenot served in these mission territories, often under conditions of great difficulty and cultural distance.

His career represented the French Catholic missionary tradition that was both inseparable from colonial power and genuinely motivated by religious conviction. Post-colonial reassessments of this history have complicated the picture: French missionaries created lasting Catholic institutions in former colonies while also participating in colonial power structures that had destructive consequences for indigenous peoples and cultures.
